_doc: Beat-by-beat visual plan for Frank Olson first 30 seconds (hook). Every visual answers: what is the narrator saying RIGHT NOW?
_principle: NO generic stock photos. Real archival + narrative-specific animations + story-driven SFX.

beats.narration: November 28, 1953. New York City. 3:09 in the morning.

visual.description: Dark aerial view of 1950s Manhattan skyline at night. City lights glowing. Camera slowly pushes in toward midtown hotel district.

text_overlay.note: Date appears with typewriter effect, sets the era immediately

sfx.note: Low distant traffic hum, 1950s urban atmosphere. Very quiet. Source from Freesound/Pixabay audio.

beats.music: Dark piano begins, barely audible — single low notes
beats.why: Establish time, place, atmosphere. Viewer sees exactly where this happened.

beats.narration: [PAUSE:0.8] A man crashes through a closed window on the 10th floor of the Hotel Statler

visual.description: Cut to Hotel Statler exterior at night. Looking UP at the building from street level. One window on the 10th floor is lit. Everything else is dark.
visual.fallback_description: Animated hotel facade — tall dark building, single lit window high up. Art deco style, 1950s New York. Dark blue/black color palette.

sub_beats.why: The pause builds dread. Viewer sees the window BEFORE the narrator describes what happens.

sub_beats.narration_words: A man crashes through a closed window

visual.description: At the word 'crashes' — QUICK CUT to close-up of shattering glass. Shards flying outward toward camera. Motion blur. This should be an animated sequence: venetian blind fragments, glass fragments, a dark silhouette figure behind them.

elements: dark silhouette of falling figure behind glass
animation_spec.note: This is THE signature visual moment. Must be impactful. Can be composited from multiple layers in Pillow: dark background + glass shard overlay + silhouette.

visual.note: Brief camera shake effect (2-3 frame jitter) to sell the impact

sfx.note: CRITICAL SFX — must be a real glass shattering sound, not a generic impact. Needs to sound like a large window.

sub_beats.why: The most important moment in the first 30 seconds. The narrator says 'crashes through a window' and the viewer SEES and HEARS the glass shatter. This is what was completely missing in v7.

sub_beats.narration_words: on the 10th floor of the Hotel Statler

visual.description: Wide shot of Hotel Statler exterior. Text overlay appears: 'HOTEL STATLER'. Camera slowly tilts up toward the 10th floor.
visual.fallback_description: Art deco hotel facade with 'HOTEL STATLER' sign. Night. 1950s architectural style.

sfx.note: Fading tinkling of glass settling. Tail end of the shatter.

sub_beats.why: Give the location a name. Viewer now knows WHERE.

beats.narration: [BEAT] and falls to his death on the pavement below. His name is Frank Olson.

sub_beats.narration_words: and falls to his death on the pavement below

visual.description: Animated downward motion — camera looking DOWN the side of the building at night. Street lamps far below. The sense of falling. Dark, vertiginous.

elements: building facade rushing past (dark bricks, lit windows)
animation_spec.technique: pan_down at high speed (25%/sec) on a tall building composite image
animation_spec.note: Can be achieved with a VERY fast pan_down on a tall building exterior image. Ken Burns at 25%/sec downward.

sfx.download_query: heavy body impact thud ground fall
sfx.note: Dull, heavy impact. NOT cartoonish. Realistic and unsettling.

sub_beats.why: The viewer experiences the fall. The fast downward pan gives a visceral sense of the 10-story drop.

visual.description: CUT TO BLACK for 0.3 seconds (the impact). Then: Frank Olson's name in white serif text on dark background, slowly revealing. If a public domain photo of Olson exists, show it. Otherwise: government-ID-style frame with his name, year of birth (1910), and 'U.S. ARMY BIOCHEMIST' below.

elements: Fade in: white serif text 'FRANK OLSON' centered
Optional: government ID photo frame (empty or with photo if available)
animation_spec.note: This is a solemn, memorial-style reveal. Simple white text on near-black. The name matters — it's the first time we hear it.

visual.note: No motion on the name card. Let it breathe.

sub_beats.music: Piano holds single low note. Silence around the name.
sub_beats.why: After the violent fall, SILENCE and a name. The contrast is powerful. Now the viewer knows this is about a real person.

beats.narration: He's 43 years old. A bacteriologist. A government scientist. A husband. The father of three young children who are at home asleep in Maryland right now, waiting for their dad to come back.
beats.note: This is a long segment (11.7s). Needs 2-3 visual cuts to match the narration arc: scientist → family man.

sub_beats.narration_words: He's 43 years old. A bacteriologist. A government scientist.

visual.description: Fort Detrick laboratory — 1940s/1950s era. Scientists in white coats working in a biological research facility. If no real photo available: a well-composed animation showing a lab interior with microscopes, test tubes, the feel of government science in the early Cold War.
alt_queries: biological warfare laboratory United States Army

text_overlay.note: Location label appears briefly — tells the viewer where Olson worked

sub_beats.why: Establish who Olson was — a government scientist. Real lab imagery grounds the story in reality.

sub_beats.narration_words: A husband. The father of three young children who are at home asleep in Maryland right now, waiting for their dad to come back.

visual.description: 1950s American family — father, mother, three children. Suburban home. Warm golden tones (contrast with the cold night we just saw). This should feel like safety, normalcy, warmth — everything that's about to be destroyed.
visual.color_note: Slightly warmer color grade here — golden/amber tint. This is the ONE warm moment in the whole video.

sub_beats.music: Piano melody becomes slightly warmer, more melodic — then cuts
sub_beats.why: The narrator says 'father of three children' — the viewer SEES children. This is what was completely missing in v7. The emotional gut punch: this man had a family, and they're waiting for him to come home.

beats.narration: And the U.S. government is about to spend the next 22 years lying about how he died. [PAUSE:3.0]

sub_beats.narration_words: And the U.S. government is about to spend the next 22 years lying about how he died.

visual.description: Close-up of a REAL declassified MKUltra document — heavy black redactions, CIA letterhead, TOP SECRET stamp. Slow zoom into the redacted sections.
visual.note: We already have these downloaded. Use the real declassified docs — they're far more powerful than any stock photo.
visual.focal_point: TOP SECRET stamp and redaction marks

text_overlay.note: The number appears as the narrator says it — visual reinforcement

sfx.note: Low rumble building underneath — dread. Use existing assets/sfx/rumble_01.mp3

sub_beats.why: '22 years lying' while looking at real classified documents. The viewer sees the actual machinery of the cover-up.

visual.description: Slow fade to black. Total darkness. Hold for 3 seconds. This is the dramatic pause that signals: 'what you're about to hear will change everything you thought you knew.'
visual.note: This silence is as important as any visual. Let the weight of '22 years lying' sink in.

sfx.note: Not dead silence — very faint room tone so it doesn't feel like a technical error

sub_beats.why: The 3-second pause is Fern's signature move. After a devastating reveal, SILENCE. Let the viewer absorb it.

must_download.description: Hotel Statler / Hotel Pennsylvania NYC exterior, 1950s era

must_create_animations.description: Glass window shattering outward — the hotel crash moment
must_create_animations.technique: Pillow composite: dark blue background + white glass shard shapes + venetian blind lines + dark silhouette

must_create_animations.description: Fast downward pan on building exterior — the 10-story fall
must_create_animations.technique: Ken Burns pan_down at 25%/sec on a tall building image

must_create_animations.description: Frank Olson memorial card — name, dates, title
must_create_animations.technique: Pillow: white serif text centered on near-black background

must_download_sfx.note: This is the single most important SFX in the entire video

must_download_sfx.description: Heavy body hitting pavement from height
must_download_sfx.search_query: heavy impact thud fall body ground
city night ambient quiet traffic distant

already_have.used_for: The classified document during '22 years lying'

editorial_notes.pacing: The first 30 seconds has 3 distinct emotional phases: DREAD (0-4s, dark city), VIOLENCE (4-10s, the crash and fall), HUMANITY (10-25s, who was this man), BETRAYAL (25-32s, the lie). Each phase has a different color temperature and energy level.
color_progression: 4-10s: Flash of white (breaking glass) then blue-black
18-25s: Warm amber/gold (family — the ONE warm moment)
25-32s: Cold blue into total black (the cover-up)
editorial_notes.cut_rhythm: 7 visual cuts in 32 seconds = 13.1 cuts/min. Matches Fern's measured 13.2/min. But every cut is motivated: location→crash→fall→name→scientist→family→document→silence
editorial_notes.music_arc: Single piano notes → brief warmth during family → silence. Music supports but never dominates.
editorial_notes.what_v7_got_wrong: v7 showed a generic statue zooming in while the narrator described Frank Olson falling from a window. The viewer saw NOTHING related to what was being said. This plan ensures every frame answers: what is the narrator saying RIGHT NOW?
